Analizde kadın işsizlik oranı, ücretli çalışan kadınların toplam kadın istihdamındaki payı, kadınlarda erken okul terk oranı, kamu eğitim harcamaları, kişi başına reel GSYH ve enflasyon açıklayıcı değişken olarak kullanılmıştır. Yatay kesit bağımlılığı ve eğim katsayılarındaki heterojenlik dikkate alınarak Genişletilmiş Ortalama Grup (AMG) tahmincisinden yararlanılmıştır. Panel geneli bulguları, kadın işsizlik oranı ile erken okul terk oranındaki artışların kadın NEET oranını anlamlı biçimde yükselttiğini göstermektedir. Ücretli çalışan kadınların payı da beklenenin aksine pozitif ve anlamlı bulunmuştur. Buna karşılık kamu eğitim harcamaları, kişi başına reel GSYH ve enflasyonun panel genelindeki etkileri istatistiksel olarak anlamlı değildir. Ülke bazındaki sonuçlar, değişkenlerin etkilerinin farklılaştığını ortaya koymaktadır. Bu bulgular, kadın NEET oranlarının incelenen ekonomik ve eğitim göstergelerinin yanı sıra bakım sorumlulukları, toplumsal cinsiyet rolleri ve işgücü piyasasının kurumsal özellikleri gibi modele dâhil edilmeyen sosyal ve yapısal faktörlerden de etkilenebileceğine işaret etmektedir. Dolayısıyla, erken okul terkini önleyen ve genç kadınların nitelikli istihdama geçişini destekleyen ülkeye özgü politikaların geliştirilmesi önem taşımaktadır.

tittel: PENGALAMAN REMAJA PUTUS SEKOLAH DALAM MENGIKUTI KONSELING DI DAERAH PARIT PEKIR BANGKA BELITUNG
kilde: PAEDAGOGY Jurnal Ilmu Pendidikan dan Psikologi
sammendrag: ABSTRACT The phenomenon of school dropouts among adolescents in Parit Pekir presents a psychosocial complexity that demands a profound understanding of their lived experiences when accessing psychological support. This study aims to delineate the experiences and meanings attributed to guidance and counseling services by school dropouts at SMK Yapensu Sungailiat through the lens of Alfred Schutz’s social phenomenology. Data collection relied on in-depth interviews, observation, and documentary study involving six adolescent school dropouts and two guidance and counseling teachers as supporting informants. Data analysis was executed cyclically, encompassing data condensation, thematic presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings reveal a significant shift in meaning; the informants' initial perception shadowed by fear and the stigma of the counseling room as a corrective-punitive space transformed into positive acceptance. Counselor interactions characterized by empathy, openness, and a non-judgmental stance cultivated a safe space that alleviated emotional turmoil while fostering the informants' self-efficacy. This study concludes that counseling for out-of-school adolescents plays a pivotal role as an intersubjective vehicle to reconstruct self-understanding and redesign future orientations. Community-based psychosocial support emerges as a crucial necessity to ensure the sustainable emotional recovery of marginalized adolescents. ABSTRAK Fenomena putus sekolah pada remaja di Parit Pekir menghadirkan kompleksitas psikososial yang menuntut pemahaman mendalam mengenai pengalaman mereka saat mengakses pendampingan psikologis. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguraikan pengalaman dan pemaknaan layanan bimbingan konseling oleh remaja putus sekolah di SMK Yapensu Sungailiat melalui lensa fenomenologi sosial Alfred Schutz. Pengumpulan data mengandalkan wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan studi dokumentasi terhadap enam remaja putus sekolah serta dua guru bimbingan konseling sebagai informan pendukung. Analisis data dijalankan secara siklis meliputi kondensasi data, penyajian tematik, serta penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian mengungkapkan pergeseran pemaknaan yang signifikan; persepsi awal informan yang dibayangi rasa takut dan stigma ruang bimbingan sebagai arena korektif-punitif bertransformasi menjadi penerimaan positif. Interaksi konselor yang empati, terbuka, dan tidak menghakimi (non-judgmental) menciptakan ruang aman (safe space) yang meredakan gejolak emosional sekaligus membangkitkan efikasi diri (self-efficacy) informan. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa konseling bagi remaja di luar sistem sekolah berperan penting sebagai wahana intersubjektif untuk merekonstruksi pemahaman diri dan merancang kembali orientasi masa depan. Pendampingan psikososial berbasis komunitas (community-based counseling) menjadi kebutuhan krusial guna menjamin keberlanjutan pemulihan emosional remaja marjinal.

tittel: Health-related labour market outcomes among migrants and natives in Finland
sammendrag: International migration is transforming the labour markets and social security systems of high-income countries. Net immigration drives population growth in Finland, with more than one in 10 employed individuals now being migrants. The native share in the working-age population is decreasing due to aging and low fertility rates. This makes migrants’ long-term employment prospects more crucial to the fiscal sustainability of the welfare state and to the maintenance of an adequate labour supply. When health issues cause migrants to leave the labour market early – whether through earnings losses, extended sick leave, or disability pensions – Finland loses valuable workers and sees an increase in the number of benefit recipients. This undermines the economic justification for labour migration. Although research on migrant labour market integration has extensively studied obstacles to employment – such as limited recognition of foreign qualifications, language barriers, and discrimination – the economic impacts of health shocks and indicators of work incapacity, including sickness absence and disability pensions, have also been explored in various contexts. However, research on how health affects migrants’ long-term work ability and work participation, and how occupational class determines these outcomes, remains scarce, particularly in Finland. To address these knowledge gaps, this dissertation shifts the focus from labour market entry to the sustainability of employment, examining how health-related career disruptions determine migrants’ long-term labour market outcomes and whether Finland’s universal welfare system provides equal protection when health deteriorates. The dissertation offers new evidence in three areas. First, it provides the first population-wide analysis of migrant–native earnings differences following acute health shocks. Second, it examines how occupational class and diagnostic groups shape patterns of sickness absence differently for migrants and natives over a 15 year period. Third, it presents the first Finnish register-based study of disability pension risk among migrants, including the role of occupational class. The dissertation develops an integrated framework that combines health and disability research, labour market stratification theory, and administrative burden theory. To explain how migrants’ structural occupational positions influence their health related labour market outcomes, this framework, drawing on and extending existing literature, identifies three mechanisms: differential exposure, differential buffering, and differential gatekeeping. The analyses of the dissertation studies were based on high-quality, full population administrative register data from 2005 to 2019. Study I employs a dynamic difference-in-differences event-study approach with entropy balancing. Study II analyses age-adjusted sickness absence prevalence and, using modified Poisson regression models with a log link function, it estimates risk ratios by occupational class, diagnostic group, and time. Study III uses Cox proportional hazards models to estimate the risk of receiving disability pensions among migrants and natives. In Study I, it was observed that health shocks resulted in substantial and persistent earnings losses. Overall, migrants lost 13.5% of their yearly earnings, compared with 7.4% for natives. Migrant men experienced the largest penalty at 17.7%, roughly twice that of migrant women (8.6%). Among migrants, those from European and Western countries as well as those from Russia or the former Soviet Union, experienced the most significant earnings declines. Social benefits compensated roughly half of natives’ earnings losses but only a third of migrants’ losses, indicating that Finland’s welfare state better buffers natives’ earnings. Study II found that, unlike earlier research from Sweden and Norway, migrants in Finland had lower sickness absence prevalence than natives across all diagnostic groups and throughout the study period. Occupational disparities in sickness absences were clear, especially among migrants, and they grew over time. By 2019, unemployed migrant men had the highest risk of all-cause (RR 2.56) and mental disorder-related sickness absence (RR 2.60) within their own group, and a risk comparable to that of manual workers for musculoskeletal sickness absence (RR 4.45). Over time, migrant men experienced a higher increase in the risk of mental disorders-related sickness absence compared to women. Study III found that migrants, compared to natives, had a lower risk of receiving a disability pension. The analysis indicated a 37% higher risk for migrants from refugee-origin countries and a 30% higher risk for those from other non-European countries compared to natives. Among all migrants, the risk of a disability pension was increased with longer residence in Finland. Differences in occupational class significantly influenced the risk of receiving a disability pension for both migrants and natives, but the gap between migrants and natives in the risk was not fully explained by occupational class. The findings of the dissertation suggested that health-related labour market disadvantages among migrants may not originate from migrant status itself but from the structurally shaped occupational positions they tend to occupy in segmented labour markets that are characterized by physically demanding work, job insecurity, and unequal access to welfare institutions. Despite Finland’s universal welfare state system, formal rights do not guarantee equal protection in practice. The dissertation concludes that long-term health-related labour market outcomes are best understood through the lens of sustainability, that is, the capacity to maintain work and earnings when health problems arise. Policy responses should target the occupational health gap within Finland’s three-channel healthcare system, adapt return-to-work tools for non-full-time jobs, and broaden integration monitoring to incorporate health-related metrics.

tittel: Investigating the perceptions of the relationship between vocational education and the labour market: a case study of FET college students
sammendrag: The study sought to investigate the perceptions of TVET students regarding vocational education and its relation to the labour market. It hoped to illuminate connections or disconnections between vocational education and employment. The research emanated from the prevailing view that TVET education by its very nature is work-oriented and therefore those who enroll in TVET colleges are able to find employment. Furthermore, that conceptually the TVET curriculum was and continues to be regarded as skills-based for labour market demands thereby enhancing national competiveness and economic growth. Qualitative questionnaires, which are open-ended in nature, were used to gather facts about students’ beliefs and experiences regarding certain engineering programmes and services offered at TVET colleges. Non-probability sampling was used to select one hundred and thirteen (113) participants who voluntarily completed qualitative questionnaires, which were structured to elicit the required information, and the results reveal divergent views shared by students. There are those who feel very strongly that a TVET qualification, in engineering in particular, leads to employment due to its demand and the fact that the institution generally assists students through the placement unit makes it even easier to find employment. Other students firmly believed that whatever qualifications one attained, the world of work cannot accommodate them, as they do not have work experience. They felt this was unfair because they are unable to find employment without being properly monitored and trained by the very same industry that hopes to employ them in the near future. They argue that the only problem pertaining to unemployment is job scarcity, rather than skills scarcity. The research is framed within the human capital theory. Research findings reveal the fact that there is no link between vocational education and the labour market and as a result employment is not easy. There are personal skills required but they are not available in our educational curriculum, which focuses on educational aspirations. The research further posits five distinct but necessary interventions that students are suggesting in order to increase their lack of experience in the job market.

tittel: Tekijät, jotka suojaavat lasta vanhemman päihteiden käytöltä ja asiat, joiden olisi koettu auttavan : Teema-analyysi muistelmateoksista
sammendrag: Tässä pro gradu -tutkielmassa tarkastelen muistelmateosten kautta tekijöitä, jotka suojaavat lasta vanhemman päihteiden käytöltä sekä tekijöitä, joiden olisi toivottu olevan lapsuudessa toisin. Päihteiden käyttö ei vaikuta vain niiden käyttäjään itseensä, vaan sen haitat ulottuvat myös muihin ihmisiin ja yhteiskuntaan. Perheissä, joissa vanhempi tai vanhemmat käyttävät päihteitä, ovat lapset erityisen alttiita näille haitoille ja vaikutuksille. Teorialuvuissa tarkastelen päihteiden käyttöä ja riippuvuutta ilmiönä Suomessa sekä tuon esille, millaisia palveluita päihteiden käyttäjille ja heidän läheisilleen on tarjolla. Aiemmassa tutkimuksessa on todettu, että lapset pyrkivät suojautumaan vanhemman päihteiden käytön vaikutuksilta monin eri tavoin. Lasta suojaavat tekijät voivat olla persoonallisuuden piirteisiin liittyviä tai lapsen omaan toimintaan pohjautuvia. Resilienssi, joka ilmenee ajattelutavoissa ja persoonallisuuden piirteiden kautta, voi osaltaan selittää, miksi vaikeissakin olosuhteissa kasvaneet lapset pystyvät säilyttämään tasapainon. Suojaavien tekijöiden voidaan nähdä tukevan resilienssiä ja sen kehittymistä. Ne ilmenevät yksilötasolla ja perheen, yhteisön ja yhteiskunnan tasoilla. Tutkimuskysymykseni ovat: 1) Millaiset tekijät tai toiminta ovat suojanneet lapsuudessa vanhemman päihteiden käytön haitallisilta vaikutuksilta ja 2) millaiset tekijät olisivat voineet auttaa lapsuudessa vähentämään vanhemman päihteiden käytön vaikutuksia? Aineistonani on kolme muistelmateosta lapsuudesta. Näissä teoksissa vahvana teemana on selviytyminen vanhemman päihteiden käytöstä huolimatta. Aineistoa analysoin laadullisesti. Analyysimenetelmänä käytän teoriasidonnaista teema-analyysiä. Analyysiä ohjaavana teoriana hyödynnän resilienssin viisiosaista mallia, joka kuvaa resilienssin muodostuvan viidestä osa-alueesta, kognitioista, tunteista, käyttäytymismalleista, fyysisestä toiminnasta ja ympäristöstä, johon sisältyvät tuki perheeltä, yhteisöltä ja yhteiskunnalta. Tutkielmani tulokset osoittavat, että lapsilla on hyvin monenlaisia suojaavia tekijöitä vanhemman päihteiden käytön vaikutuksia vastaan. Lasta suojaavat tekijät jakautuvat tulosten perusteella lapsen sisäisiin ominaisuuksiin, kuten ajattelutapoihin, tunteisiin ja käyttäytymiseen liittyviin sekä ulkoisiin tekijöihin, johon sisältyy tuki perheeltä, yhteisöltä ja yhteiskunnalta. Kertomusten valossa lapset näyttäytyvät aktiivisina toimijoina, joiden lapsuutta varjostaa kuitenkin monenlaiset tunteet ja velvollisuudet. Tulosten perusteella voidaan myös tunnistaa tekijöitä, joiden olisi toivottu lapsuudessa olevan toisin. Nämä tekijät ovat sellaisia, jotka olisivat auttaneet lasta, mutta eivät todellisuudessa toteutuneet. Tällaiset tekijät jakautuvat kertomuksissa perustarpeiden täyttämiseen, johon sisältyvät esimerkiksi ruoka, turvallisuus ja rakkaus sekä pettymykseen yhteiskunnan ja ammattilaisten toimintatapoihin ja asenteisiin. Tulokseni ovat yhteydessä aiemman tutkimuksen ajatukseen siitä, että lapsi voidaan nähdä aktiivisena toimijana, jolla on taito ja pyrkimys suojautua vanhemman päihteiden käytöltä eri tavoin. Jatkotutkimuksen kannalta olisi hedelmällistä selvittää, miten ammattilaiset tunnistavat lasta suojaavia tekijöitä ja miten he pystyvät tukemaan näitä työskennellessään lasten ja perheiden kanssa. Lisäksi tärkeää olisi selvittää lasten kohdatuksi tulemista palveluissa.

tittel: Gendered academic persistence in engineering education: bibliometric trends and underlying mechanisms
Tracking Urbanisation Gradient of NEET: Trends and Changing Rural-Urban Gaps
Overqualification in European labour markets: Club convergence and its determinants
sammendrag: This study examines the evolution of overqualification across 28 European countries and investigates the macroeconomic and labour market factors shaping its persistence and cross-country differences. Using the Phillips–Sul club convergence methodology, we show that young workers in Europe exhibit multiple convergence paths, while experienced workers tend to converge towards a common equilibrium. We then identify the characteristics associated with convergence club membership using an ordered probit model and examine the short-run determinants of overqualification through a System GMM dynamic panel framework with regional interactions. The results highlight substantial heterogeneity across European labour markets: overqualification is persistent over time, and the effects of unemployment and unemployment benefits on skill mismatch vary between northern and peripheral European economies. These findings suggest that overqualification is shaped not only by individual characteristics but also by labour market institutions and macroeconomic conditions, with important implications for education, employment, and skills-matching policies in Europe.

tittel: Efficient stabilizer or deadweight effect? The impact of subsidies for apprenticeship training during an economic downturn
sammendrag: Economic downturns often come along with a reduction of apprenticeship training by firms, hereby threatening economies with a lack of skilled labour in the mid- and long-run. Against this background, the German government has implemented an apprenticeship subsidy for small and medium sized companies in the summer of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. In brief, companies that maintained their number of new apprenticeships at the average level of the past three years could receive €2000 for each apprenticeship starting in the autumn of 2020. We exploit eligibility for the subsidy due to firm size and compare eligible and non-eligible firms in an intent-to-treat difference-in-differences (DiD) design. The estimates show no impact on the number of new apprenticeships but a moderate effect on the probability to maintain the training level at the level of the past three years. This suggests that firms that were at the margin of maintaining the level without the subsidy have hired a small number of additional apprentices to receive the subsidy. This mirrors the incentive structure of the subsidy, as firms at the margin have received a large amount of money for a small number of additional apprenticeships. These results are robust to a wide range of sensitivity and robustness checks, including linear and non-linear DiD estimation, tests for diverging trends, placebo tests with placebo outcomes as well as checks for panel attrition. These results add to the scarce literature on the impact of training subsidies in general and their impact during economic crises in particular.

tittel: Completion Rates and the Time It Takes to Earn a Degree in Community College Bachelor's Programs
kilde: ResearchWorks at the University of Washington (University of Washington)
sammendrag: One of the intents of a community college bachelor’s degree (CCB) program is to smooth the pathway to a bachelor’s degree and into the workforce for community college students, reducing the time it takes these students to earn a degree and, as a result, lowering the overall cost. However, there is limited research on the extent to which these goals are achieved, and for whom. Using a comprehensive dataset from Washington, this brief examines the completion rates, time to degree, and, by extension, affordability of CCB programs. Findings include: -- After two years, about half of CCB students graduate with a bachelor’s degree (46%). The three-year completion rates jump by 14% percentage points to 60% and steadily grow to 64%, 67%, and 71% by four, five, and six years after entry, respectively. -- CCB students consistently had higher completion rates within two-, four-, and six years relative to community-college-to-traditional-university transfer students. This was true across nearly every gender, race/ethnicity, and age group examined. -- CCB students took, on average, a little over two years to complete their degrees. With a shortened time to degree and a lower cost, CCB programs are well-positioned to expand access to and achievement of the bachelor’s degree for traditionally underserved students.

tittel: Higher TVET and Occupations: Moving towards defining and understanding higher skills development
sammendrag: Context: Higher Technical and Vocational Education and Training (Higher TVET) has gained prominence in policy debates as a mechanism to enhance economic competitiveness and social mobility. However, despite its growing importance, there remains limited conceptual clarity on what constitutes “higher” skills within TVET systems and how these are developed and recognised across national contexts. Thus, this paper examines why current higher TVET systems are often unlikely to deliver on higher levels of skills development. Approach: This paper analyses literature on definitions and characteristics of Higher TVET systems using my occupational capacity conceptual framework (Alphonsus, 2023a). It analyses contradictions between policy narratives and implementation by applying the concept of occupational capacity to examine how specialised knowledge and the social organisation of work shape the development of higher skills. Findings: The analysis finds that Higher TVET is inconsistently defined and frequently conflated with short-cycle training, upskilling, and reskilling initiatives. Systems are often fragmented, with weak alignment between education provision, occupational pathways, and labour market recognition. Employer engagement is uneven, and higher vocational pathways often lack clear progression routes towards occupational expertise, consequently limiting their effectiveness in developing advanced occupational skills. Conclusion: The paper argues that Higher TVET requires reconceptualisation around coherent occupational pathways that systematically develop specialised knowledge needed for expert practice. Ultimately higher skills development requires a combination of employer recognition and participation, alongside clear occupational pathways that represent shared institutional arrangements between education systems, employers, and labour market structures.

tittel: Good Job Expectations and Submissiveness in the Labor Market among Young Adults with NEET Status
sammendrag: Purpose: The purpose of this study is to determine how family/partner financial support is associated with employment expectations (Good Job Expectations; GJE) and willingness to make concessions in the labor market (Submissiveness in the Labor Market; SI) among young adults with NEET status, while accounting for caregiving responsibilities and the duration of NEET status.Design/Methodology/Approach: A cross-sectional CAPI survey was conducted among 1074 individuals aged 18-34 who had been out of employment, education, and training for at least three months prior to participation in the study.The associations corresponding to H1 and H2 were estimated using two OLS linear regression models.Both models included family/partner financial support, caregiving responsibilities, and duration of NEET status.Findings: Family/partner financial support was positively associated with GJE and negatively associated with SI, also after accounting for the other predictors.The findings indicate that a private financial safety net co-occurs with higher expectations regarding future employment and a lower willingness to accept less favorable or more demanding employment conditions.Practical Implications: The findings suggest that labor market activation measures and employment services targeting people with NEET may take into account differences in their private financial safety nets.Individuals without such a safety net may face greater pressure to accept less favorable job offers quickly, whereas those receiving support from family or a partner may have greater scope to reject them.Originality/Value: The literature review identified no previous studies directly testing the association of current family/partner financial support simultaneously with GJE and SI among young adults with NEET status.The study therefore extends the existing literature by examining relationships between private economic

tittel: Gendered Privilege and Masculinity-Related Burdens in Manufacturing Internships: Male Vocational Students’ Workplace Learning Experiences in Indonesia
sammendrag: Gender research in vocational education has primarily examined women’s exclusion, while male students’ experiences of privilege and masculinity-related pressure remain underexplored. This study examined how male vocational students experienced gender-based privilege, encountered psychological and pedagogical burdens, and interpreted their relationship during manufacturing internships. The study employed a qualitative design informed by a constructivist–interpretivist paradigm and Masculinity Studies, particularly Connell’s relational approach to masculinities. The study analyzed semi-structured interviews with 61 male students from two vocational secondary schools in Bekasi, Indonesia, using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants reported that gendered expectations associating men with strength, readiness, courage, and independence facilitated early access to core technical tasks, supervisory trust, and valuable learning opportunities. The same expectations intensified performance demands, physical workloads, risk exposure, restricted help-seeking, and limited pedagogical support. Participants interpreted this position through normalization, ambivalence, and critical reflection. Some proposed competency-based task allocation, equitable supervision, and safer learning environments. The study introduces conditional access privilege as a gendered position in which access to valuable technical learning resources must be maintained through masculine performance, generating psychological pressure and pedagogical vulnerability. The findings support internship practices that separate competency assessment, task allocation, supervision, and learning support from gendered expectations.

tittel: An investigation into the outcomes of articulation agreements between South African Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges and universities for students in Engineering Studies.
kilde: UWC Research Repository (University of the Western Cape)
sammendrag: This doctoral thesis offers a critical analysis of how articulation agreements between South African Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges and Universities of Technology (UoTs) are enacted and experienced, with a specific focus on engineering pathways. Despite the presence of national frameworks such as the National Qualifications Framework (NQF) and the Articulation Policy (DHET, 2017a), persistent disconnects remain between policy intentions and the actual lived experience of students transitioning from TVET to higher education. Existing research frequently documents misalignments between policy and institutional practice but rarely investigates the underlying systemic, cultural, and relational dynamics or foregrounds student voices in shaping these transitions. This study addresses this critical gap by asking: How have articulation agreements between TVET colleges and universities been enacted, and what have been the outcomes of such agreements for students and institutions? The research is anchored in an interpretivist, qualitative case study methodology, combining semi-structured interviews with staff and focus group discussions with engineering students across three UoTs. The analytical framework integrates Ecological Systems Theory with Relational Agency Theory, providing a nuanced lens to examine how multiple levels, such as policy, institution, staff, and individual, interact in the articulation process. Findings uncover a complex reality: while formal pathways exist on paper, effective articulation is often undermined by fragmented curricula, inconsistent institutional collaboration, and limited recognition of TVET qualifications by university staff. Notably, the success of many articulation arrangements rests precariously on the efforts of “articulation champions”, who are dedicated individuals whose advocacy is vital, but whose absence exposes systemic vulnerability. Student narratives reveal multiple challenges across the academic, administrative, and psychosocial realms, with many navigating intricate admission and credit-transfer processes in the absence of coherent support systems. The thesis concludes that achieving equitable educational transitions demands more than compliance with policy: it requires systemic alignment, robust inter-institutional partnerships, ongoing staff development, and the institutionalisation of holistic student support. This research reframes articulation not merely as a policy or pipeline issue, but as an ecological and relational process that is dynamic, context-dependent, and deeply human. Actionable recommendations are provided for policymakers, institutional leaders, practitioners, and future researchers, including the need for ii https://uwcscholar.uwc.ac.za/homeembedded articulation support structures, targeted professional development, and longitudinal research tracking student outcomes. In doing so, the study not only fills a critical gap in the South African literature but also sets an international research and practice agenda that prioritises lived experience and multi-level agency as central to educational policy transformation.

tittel: Trapped in a Gray Zone of Isolation: A Qualitative Study on the Social Withdrawal and Isolation Experiences of Youth NEETs in South Korea
sammendrag: Young people not in employment, education, or training (hereafter, Youth NEETs) have been examined in South Korea primarily through quantitative indicators, leaving the lived experience of their social isolation and withdrawal largely unexplored. This study explored how Korean Youth NEETs experience isolation and withdrawal, and how these states are formed and sustained within their life contexts. A qualitative multiple-case study was conducted with eight non-job-seeking Youth NEETs aged 19-34, recruited purposively in Seoul. Data were collected through repeated in-depth interviews and were analyzed through within-case analysis followed by Stake's cross-case analysis. Five main categories, 11 subcategories, and 33 meaning units emerged: the shadow of marginalization; being pushed out into the world unprepared; being treated as expendable in an unstable labor market; failing on the high threshold of employment; and being trapped in a gray zone of isolation. Participants experienced cumulative and multidimensional social exclusion across family, school, the labor market, and social relationships, which manifested psycho-emotionally as learned helplessness, self-stigma, avoidant coping, and depressive distress. The findings suggest that NEET status should be reframed as a problem of multidimensional social exclusion rather than individual failure, and that integrated, stage-based psycho-emotional support is needed alongside employment-centered policies.

tittel: A longitudinal perspective on educational inequalities in Romania: between-cohort comparisons and within-cohort progression across stages and pathways
sammendrag: Introduction Progression through educational milestones and inequality need not change in parallel: group differences may narrow at one transition, widen at another, or shift into differentiated pathways. Methods Using Romanian administrative records, we compared the 1999, 2004, and 2009 birth cohorts across six transition-specific analyses in two overlapping historical windows. A linked stage-based multi-state analysis followed 122,344 students in the 2004 cohort from a documented Grade 5 origin through Baccalaureate success within four examination opportunities. We estimated model-implied probabilities and probability differences by sex, the Roma administrative marker, first language, and school setting. Results The later cohort had higher probabilities at four milestones: promoted Grade 8 completion [2009 vs. 2004: +4.11 percentage points (pp)], promoted Grade 12 completion within day-school high school (2004 vs. 1999: +7.16 pp), Baccalaureate entry (+2.33 pp), and Baccalaureate success within the first two examination opportunities (+7.60 pp). Group differences changed unevenly: female–male differences were smaller in the later cohort at all four milestones, non-Roma–Roma differences narrowed at Grade 8 and Grade 12 completion, whereas the urban–rural difference narrowed at Grade 12 completion and Baccalaureate success but widened at Baccalaureate entry. Grade 9 pathway composition varied by cohort and group. Within the linked 2004 cohort, standardized probabilities from Grade 5 were 90.54% for promoted Grade 8 completion, 64.59% for documented high-school completion, 60.21% for Baccalaureate entry, and 50.72% for Baccalaureate success through four examination opportunities. Between Grade 8 completion and Baccalaureate success within the first four examination opportunities, the female–male gap increased from 0.67 to 15.08 pp, the non-Roma–Roma gap from 30.75 to 43.15 pp, the Romanian–different-first-language gap from 0.79 to 6.21 pp, and the urban–rural Grade 5-origin gap from 2.32 to 30.39 pp; not all gaps evolved monotonically across stages. Discussion Aggregate progression, between-cohort change in inequality, and inequality development across stages within a cohort are related but distinct processes. A single endpoint can obscure convergence at some transitions alongside larger or reconfigured inequalities elsewhere in the educational trajectory. Stage-sensitive longitudinal evidence can identify where inequalities become most pronounced and guide research on their mechanisms and intervention effectiveness.

tittel: Explainable AI for Student Dropout Prediction: A Hierarchical LightGBM Approach
kilde: Jurnal RESTI (Rekayasa Sistem dan Teknologi Informasi)
sammendrag: The high dropout rate in health science programs not only affects the efficiency of educational management but also threatens the stability of the professional medical workforce. This research proposes a Hierarchical Early Warning System (HEWS) framework using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm to predict student dropout risks at an early stage, utilizing a primary dataset of academic and demographic records from an Indonesian health sciences faculty. While previous studies predominantly utilized full-trajectory academic records, this study compares the model's performance across two temporal scenarios: early detection using historical data up to the second semester and full-trajectory evaluation. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is applied to address the extreme class imbalance inherent in educational datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an F1-Score of 0.95 for the minority class in both internal scenarios and maintains a robust F1-Score of 0.91 when validated against an international dataset. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is integrated to dissect the algorithm's black-box nature. The SHAP analysis reveals a critical shift in risk drivers: high school education quality and first-semester grades dominate the early detection phase, whereas fourth-semester grades and sick leave frequencies become primary predictors in the full-trajectory phase. These findings provide actionable insights for university management to design targeted academic and psychological interventions, thereby supporting the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 3 and 4.

tittel: The Relationship Between Earning Dual Enrollment Credits and Saving Time and Money in Undergraduate Degree Completion at a Christian College
kilde: Journal of Research on Christian Education
sammendrag: Dual enrollment programs are billed as valuable preparation for success in college and often promote opportunities for reduced time and expense in college-degree completion. However, there appears to be a lack of research actually supporting, or disproving, these claims of profitability. This research used a quantitative, correlational study to evaluate the predictive relationship between the number of dual enrollment credits earned by students while in high school and the subsequent length of time to college degree completion. The sample included 103 undergraduate students pursuing a baccalaureate degree at Midwestern, private, nonprofit, religious university. Utilizing self-reported demographic data and measures derived through the Graduating Student Survey (GSS), a multiple regression analysis revealed no statistically significant relationship based on the linear combination of dual enrollment credits, anticipated college debt load, and time to degree completion. Limitations of the study include a non-diverse sampling and the use of self-reported data. Implications and recommendations for future research are provided. The authors report there are no competing interests to declare.

tittel: Neet Youth in The Kyrgyz Republic: Barriers to Labour Market Inclusion for Groups with Low Mobility
kilde: The Research Journal of Business in Emerging Economics
sammendrag: The NEET phenomenon (not engaged in labor, study, or vocational training) is one of the most acute socio-economic problems in the Kyrgyz Republic, affecting approximately one-third of young people aged 15–29. The article examines an aspect that has so far received insufficient scientific attention: the structural and spatial barriers that hinder low-mobility populations – including rural youth, young women, persons with disabilities, and internal migrants – from accessing the labor market and educational opportunities. Drawing on data from the National Statistical Committee of the Kyrgyz Republic, the International Labour Organization, and the World Bank, as well as a systematic review of peer-reviewed literature published in 2015–2024, the study reflects the multidimensional nature of exclusion in seven areas. The results show pronounced regional differences: in the southern and remote regions (Batken, Naryn, Jalal-Abad), the NEET rate exceeds 38–43%, while in Bishkek it is 23%. The study identifies six main categories of barriers: physical mobility restrictions, digital access gaps, gender and socio-normative constraints, information asymmetry, legal and institutional barriers, and economic deprivation. Based on the analysis, the article proposes a policy framework focused on digital integration of the labor market, targeted vocational training, interagency coordination, and mechanisms to support mobility. The results of the study contribute to the emerging literature on spatially differentiated exclusion of youth from the labor market in Central Asia and offer practical recommendations for policy-makers, NGOs, and international development partners working in the Kyrgyz Republic.

tittel: Financial Capability, Job Opportunities, Social Influence, and Dropout Intention among Business Administration Students
kilde: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
sammendrag: This study examined the levels of financial capability, job opportunities, and social influence, and their relationship to dropout intention among Business Administration students at selected satellite campuses of Bukidnon State University. Quantitative, descriptive, and correlational research designs were employed, using a researcher-developed questionnaire to collect data from participants. Descriptive statistics were used to determine the levels of the study variables, while Pearson Product-Moment Correlation was employed to examine their relationships with dropout intention. Results showed that participants had high levels of financial capability, job opportunities, and social influence. On the other hand, dropout intention was moderately high, with financially driven dropout intention obtaining the highest level. Financial capability was not significantly related to dropout intention, whereas job opportunities and social influence were significantly and positively related to dropout intention. These suggest that students' dropout intention is more closely associated with employment-related considerations and social influences than with their overall financial capability. The study underscores the need for responsive student support interventions addressing work-study concerns, employment decisions, and social support to strengthen educational persistence.

tittel: Dropout Intention Among Sexual Minority University Students: The Mediating Role of Academic Engagement
Analysis and Forecasting of Youth Employment: A Comparative Study between Shandong Province, China and Klang Valley, Malaysia
sammendrag: Youth labor markets in Shandong Province, China, and the Klang Valley, Malaysia, have moved from problems of job quantity to problems of structural friction, yet the two regions are usually studied with incompatible indicators and in separate literatures.This article sets out a quantitative research design for analyzing and forecasting youth employment in both regions, with NEET (not in employment, education or training) status treated as an endogenous determinant of later outcomes rather than only as a residual outcome of weak demand.Four research questions are addressed.The first establishes harmonized baselines and trends since 2014 for labor force participation, unemployment and NEET prevalence among young people aged 15 to 29, together with survey-based measures of long-term disengagement.The second asks whether the duration of disengagement is associated with psychological distress, measured with the Kessler 6 scale, and with downgraded career expectations, measured as a reservation wage gap.The third uses multi-group structural equation modeling, preceded by measurement invariance testing, to compare how perceived involution and skill mismatch shape disengagement trajectories in each region.The fourth evaluates whether adding structural employability variables, including an education and industry matching index and exposure to digital substitution, improves the explanatory power and out-of-sample accuracy of NEET forecasting models relative to a macroeconomic baseline.The design combines official and survey-based secondary series with a harmonized survey of 1,500 school leavers aged 18 to 29, 750 in each region.Decision rules, power calculations, endogeneity checks and ethical safeguards are fixed before data collection.Because the two regions publish very different youth statistics, the article also shows how a comparison can be built when official series are missing or not comparable, and it sets out how the resulting models can be used for exante policy scenarios.

tittel: The Implementation of Education Policy and Its Impact on the Quality of Human Resources in Batam City, Indonesia
sammendrag: This study examines the implementation of education policy in Batam City and its implications for human resource quality amid rapid industrial development. As one of Indonesia’s major industrial hubs, Batam faces increasing demand for skilled workers, while a persistent mismatch remains between educational outcomes and the competencies required by local industries. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, this study analyzed education policy implementation through documentation studies and a review of relevant education policies, focusing on vocational education, teacher competency, education–industry linkages, and labor-market relevance. The findings revealed challenges, including uneven educational infrastructure, disparities in teacher competency, limited industry exposure among vocational teachers, weak coordination between educational institutions and industry, and insufficient alignment between vocational curricula and changing industrial skill requirements. This study contributes to the literature by developing an industry-oriented perspective on education policy implementation in an industrial city, demonstrating that education–industry mismatch is not merely a curriculum problem but also an institutional and governance issue. The study highlights the importance of industry-based teacher development, industry-informed vocational curricula, structured student internships, and systematic graduate employment tracking. By connecting education policy with Batam’s industrial and geographical characteristics, this study extends discussions of education–industry alignment. It demonstrates the importance of institutional coordination and labor-market responsiveness in strengthening human resource quality and supporting sustainable industrial development.

tittel: The Impact of School-Based Career Activities on Vietnamese Lower Secondary Schools Students’ Career Decision-Making Self-Efficacy
kilde: International Journal of Learning Teaching and Educational Research
sammendrag: Grounded in Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), this study investigates the relationships among school-based career guidance activities, perceived effectiveness (PE), and Career Decision-Making Self-Efficacy (CDMSE) among lower secondary school students (Grades 6–9) in Vietnam. The research disaggregates career interventions into three distinct dimensions: informational, interactive (INT), and experiential (EXP) activities. A quantitative survey was conducted with a stratified cluster sample of 4,910 lower secondary school students across seven representative provinces in Northern, Central, and Southern Vietnam, analyzed via partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (PLS-MGA). The structural model revealed that school-based activities do not automatically enhance psychological confidence. Instead, Perceived Effectiveness (PE) emerged as a substantial mediator, explaining 61.4% of the variance in CDMSE (R2 = 0.614). Informational activities exerted the highest total indirect effect, serving as an indispensable cognitive foundation to reduce vocational ambiguity. Concurrently, interactive (? = 0.101) and experiential (? = 0.095) activities demonstrated significant positive direct paths to PE. Notably, while the experiential dimension yielded a negligible direct path to CDMSE (? = 0.024, p = 0.021), its impact was driven heavily by a potent indirect path (? = 0.073, t = 5.714) filtered through PE. This underscores that raw exposure to reality loses its psychological value unless tightly coupled with intentional teacher scaffolding (pre-activity preparation and post-activity reflection). Furthermore, PLS-MGA established structural invariance across classroom tracking environments (regular vs. selective classes). These findings offer vital empirical insights for educational administrators to optimize resources and transition toward highly interactive, well-scaffolded guidance models within Vietnam's 2018 General Education Curriculum.

tittel: Completing upper secondary school: Results from a ten-year longitudinal study in Norway
sammendrag: The completion of education is important both for the individual and society. High dropout rates from upper secondary school have been a national problem in Norway, and especially in northern Norway. Academic aptitude or grades (GPA) are important, but given the multifaceted nature of dropout, we conducted a longitudinal analysis to examine predictors of school completion after ten years. The study included 1676 students in Troms County (latitude 69 degrees north) starting in upper secondary education in 2010. We included a broad set of predictors related to school performance, psychological factors such as vulnerability, resilience, personality, and mental health, alongside demographic data. The mixture modeling revealed three completion trajectories: normal progression (40.1%), delayed completion (36.6%), and non-completion (23.3%). Correlation analyses showed significant relationships between completion and several of these predictors; however, in multinomial regression analyses, no variables beyond GPA significantly predicted the normal progression trajectory, whereas delayed completion was additionally accounted for by study track choice and self-perceived health, with GPA playing an even stronger role. This underscores the importance of prior school performance, but we also discuss the implications of the findings for the delayed-completion group.

tittel: Finding the "Right Path" of Vocational Education: A Comparison Between China and European Countries
kilde: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
sammendrag: Nowadays, global economy is developing rapidly. Fast technological iteration boosts the transforming and upgrading of industries. The popularization of higher education in recent decades leads to a surge in the number of graduates with certificates. Various factors result in the fiercely competitive labor market today. As a consequence, unemployment has become a widespread difficulty faced by a large number of young people worldwide. In this case, vocational education has gradually become an effective way to relieve this problem and ensure sustainable economic growth. This article will discuss the social and systematical causes of the marginalization of vocational education in China. It will also compare Chinese system with two typical European vocational education patterns, apprenticeship in Denmark and dual system in Germany, in an attempt to find an ideal and relatively complete vocational education systems to deal with youth unemployment across societies. This article mainly uses comparative research method to analyze the differences between education systems. Several overall practical suggestions of improvement of vocational education system are also given.

tittel: A fuzzy logic decision support system for university student dropout assessment
sammendrag: Student dropout continues to be an issue in universities, which has a negative impact on the academic performance of students and the reputation of educational institutions. Since the dropout decision is affected by multiple factors like academic performance, financial situation, stress, and self-motivation, the status of these factors can be highly uncertain, subjective, and conventional assessment methods cannot consider this impreciseness. This study designed a fuzzy logic–based decision support system approach to account for the risk of student dropout in a flexible and human-like way. The purpose of this study was to assess the potential risk of a student dropout decision by taking four key input variables: Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA), Financial Stability, Stress level, and Self-motivation. The output variable of the system is Dropout Risk Level. A Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) using the Mamdani inference method was developed, which was implemented using the MATLAB Fuzzy Logic Toolbox. Each input variable was represented using three fuzzy linguistic terms (Low, Medium, and High) and triangular membership functions. Fuzzy IF–THEN rules were constructed based on the researcher’s expertise and assistance from experienced lecturers. Data were collected using structured questionnaires distributed to students.

tittel: Dynamic Models of Human Capital Accumulation
sammendrag: This dissertation consists of three separate essays that use dynamic models to better understand the human capital accumulation process. First, I analyze the role of migration in human capital accumulation and how migration varies over the business cycle. An interesting trend in the data is that, over the period of the Great Recession, overall migration rates in the US remained close to their respective long-term trends. However, migration evolved differently by employment status: unemployed workers were more likely to migrate during the recession and employed workers less likely. To isolate mechanisms explaining this divergence, I estimate a dynamic, non-stationary search model of migration using a national longitudinal survey from 2004-2013. I focus on the role of employment frictions on migration decisions in addition to other explanations in the literature. My results show that a divergence in job offer and job destruction rates caused differing migration incentives by employment status. I also find that migration rates were muted because of the national scope of the Great Recession. Model simulations show that spatial unemployment insurance in the form of a moving subsidy can help workers move to more favorable markets. In the second essay, my coauthors and I explore the role of information frictions in the acquisition of human capital. Specifically, we investigate the determinants of college attrition in a setting where individuals have imperfect information about their schooling ability and labor market productivity. We estimate a dynamic structural model of schooling and work decisions, where high school graduates choose a bundle of education and work combinations. We take into account the heterogeneity in schooling investments by distinguishing between two- and four-year colleges and graduate school, as well as science and non-science majors for four-year colleges. Individuals may also choose whether to work full-time, part-time, or not at all. A key feature of our approach is to account for correlated learning through college grades and wages, thus implying that individuals may leave or re-enter college as a result of the arrival of new information on their ability and/or productivity. We use our results to quantify the importance of informational frictions in explaining the observed school-to-work transitions and to examine sorting patterns. In the third essay, my coauthors and I investigate the evolution over the last two decades in the wage returns to schooling and early work experience. Using data from the 1979 and 1997 panels of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth, we isolate changes in skill prices from changes in composition by estimating a dynamic model of schooling and work decisions. Importantly, this allows us to account for the endogenous nature of the changes in educational and accumulated work experience over this time period. We find an increase over this period in the returns to working in high school, but a decrease in the returns to working while in college. We also find an increase in the incidence of working in college, but that any detrimental impact of in-college work experience is offset by changes in other observable characteristics. Overall, our decomposition of the evolution in skill premia suggests that both price and composition effects play an important role. The role of unobserved ability is also important.
